name: Islamic Liberalism
summary: Islamic liberalism is the strand of Muslim thought, in Kurzman's account, that combines Islam with opposition to theocracy, support for democracy, rights for women and non-Muslims, freedom of thought and belief in progress. It rests on ijtihad, the critical reinterpretation of Qur'an and law for modern conditions, and argues that a secular, rights-protecting state is good for Islam itself. Its economics are not settled, ranging from social-democratic to market-friendly.
scope: Contemporary liberal Islam as gathered in Charles Kurzman's Liberal Islam: A Sourcebook and the Wikipedia article on liberal and progressive movements within Islam, drawing on 'Ali 'Abd al-Raziq, Abdullahi An-Na'im, Abduh-style modernism, Abdolkarim Soroush and activist groups such as Muslims for Progressive Values. It excludes Islamist democrats, who keep shari'a as state law, and the fully secular critics of religion. The progressive-activist wing is more affirming on LGBTQ and gender questions than the wider liberal mainstream, so those answers are low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Abdullahi Ahmed An-Na'im
keyFigures.role: Scholar who argues on Islamic grounds for a secular state and against state enforcement of shari'a.

keyFigures.name: Ali Abdel Raziq
keyFigures.role: Egyptian scholar whose 1925 book argued that the caliphate was not obligatory and that Islam does not prescribe a political system.

keyFigures.name: Abdolkarim Soroush
keyFigures.role: Iranian philosopher who argues that religious states must be democratic and no interpretation of Islam is final.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Muslims for Progressive Values lists universal health care among its stated commitments to social justice.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal Islam has no settled economic doctrine, and its thinkers range from market-friendly modernists to socialist-leaning Shi'ites, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist Shi'ites such as Taleghani favored collective ownership while most liberal modernists did not address it, so the strand is divided.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only the Shi'ite socialist wing, such as Taleghani's collective ownership argument, endorses this; the liberal mainstream does not.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: MPV protects nonviolent expression but says free speech cannot justify hate speech or incitement; whether this should be law is left open.

strong-leader.rationale: Democratic accountability and opposition to personal or clerical rule make bypassing gridlock through a strong leader unattractive.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal Muslims such as An-Na'im want a secular, constitutional state that protects rights, so they see the state as necessary rather than harmful.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources are silent, and adherents are split between bodily-autonomy arguments and traditional moral limits.

decide-locally.rationale: Liberal Islam has no doctrine on centralization; Abduh accepted national states but no localist program is documented.

traditional-family.rationale: Liberal Muslims value family but challenge patriarchal family law, so adherents divide on the statement.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: MPV and Unity Mosque-type groups back full LGBTQ equality and inclusion, though many liberal Muslims outside them stop short of marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: MPV commits to reproductive justice; broader liberal Muslim opinion is divided and rarely stated formally.

more-religion-public.rationale: MPV and An-Na'im argue that religious and state authority should be separated, which tells against a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: MPV commits to dismantling structural racism; the broader liberal tradition says little on this.

gender-social-construct.rationale: MPV supports gender identity inclusion but liberal Islam has no doctrine on whether gender is socially constructed.

gradual-change.rationale: Abduh-style reformers were gradualist while more radical hermeneutic thinkers such as Abu Zayd were not, so the strand is split.

free-trade.rationale: No liberal Islamic source takes a position on trade policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Universal rights favor it, but many progressive Muslims are post-colonial critics of Western intervention, so the strand is split.

open-borders.rationale: Equal worth of all people points toward openness, but nothing in the sources endorses open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: MPV backs environmental justice, but there is no documented position on limiting economic growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Liberal Islam believes in human progress but the sources give no view on technology solving most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The sources contain nothing on nuclear energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: MPV rejects violence at every level and liberal Islam prefers reform through democracy, though Shariati's revolutionary line is an exception.

experts-over-public.rationale: Democracy and consent are core commitments, which weigh against giving experts more say than the public.

socialized-markets.rationale: Only the socialist Shi'ite wing addresses this, so adherents are split.

land-value-tax.rationale: No liberal Islamic source mentions land taxation.

basic-income.rationale: Anti-poverty commitments are stated but no mechanism such as basic income is discussed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kurzman defines liberal Islam by support for democracy and opposition to theocracy, which excludes ideological one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale weighs a ceremonial monarch against a ruler with real power, and the statement now asks only about a ceremonial head of state.

reviewHistory.rationale: Liberal Muslim thinkers back elected, accountable government, though some reformers accept constitutional monarchies.

democracy-best.rationale: Kurzman lists support for democracy as a defining position of liberal Islam, and these thinkers treat elected government as the legitimate basis of rule even when outcomes are unwelcome.

natural-rulers.rationale: MPV affirms the equal worth of all human beings, which rules out a natural class of rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: MPV rejects violence at the individual, organizational and national levels, though anticolonial exceptions exist.

war-builds-character.rationale: MPV's rejection of violence at the national level tells against glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: MPV states separation of religious and state authorities as a core principle, Kurzman lists church-state separation as a shared concern, and Abd al-Raziq and An-Na'im argue for it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: An-Na'im argues the state should not enforce shari'a, and Kurzman defines the tradition by opposition to theocracy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth regardless of ethnicity and nationality, which is incompatible with an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Only the socialist Shi'ite strand adopts this; liberals generally do not.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The sources stress equal opportunity and economic justice but do not take a stance on equal outcomes.

civilizational-union.rationale: Abduh held that the ummah's unity is moral rather than political, which permits separate national states.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Compassion and justice are named as the guides to all conduct, which does not fit celebrating self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: MPV commits to universal human rights and individual freedom of conscience as basic.

limit-population.rationale: MPV's emphasis on women's reproductive self-determination tells against coercive limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Liberal Islam is defined partly by belief in human progress, which contradicts this view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Progress is valued but there is no support for deliberately disrupting institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources are silent and adherents are split between liberty and religious caution.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kurzman lists belief in human progress as a defining feature and liberals reject medieval authorities' frozen readings.

direct-action.rationale: Liberals favor democratic institutions, but MPV supports nonviolent dissent so direct action is not rejected outright.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Only the socialist Shi'ite strand speaks to this, so adherents are split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim embraced only by the socialist Shi'ite wing; liberals mostly do not hold it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A dictatorship over a class contradicts the democratic and rights commitments that define liberal Islam.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist claim not found in the liberal Islamic sources.

harm-principle.rationale: Freedom of thought and conscience point toward limiting the state to preventing harm, though religious moral limits would temper it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: MPV stresses individual rights but also communal religious identity, so the sources do not settle it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democracy is the defining commitment, so voting is not subordinated to exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: MPV ties freedom to equal social, economic and educational opportunity.

hereditarian-race.rationale: MPV affirms the equal worth of all people regardless of race.

total-state.rationale: A state directing all of life is the opposite of the liberal and anti-theocratic stance defining the tradition.

bound-labor.rationale: MPV affirms equality and freedom for all, which is incompatible with legally bound labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Abu Zayd's contextual reading of the Qur'an resonates, but liberals do not generally adopt a power-based theory of knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: MPV commits to universal human rights and human equal worth across cultures.

single-common-good.rationale: MPV embraces pluralism and diversity, which tells against a single reason-derived common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources are silent, and the liberal Muslim milieu is divided, though most would not endorse a right to statehood in Palestine.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Only the socialist Shi'ite strand supports it, so the strand is divided.

school-vouchers.rationale: MPV supports public education but gives no position on vouchers.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources link political freedom to rights and democracy, not to economic freedom.

national-self-determination.rationale: Abduh accepted national states, and liberal thinkers are anti-colonial.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Abduh and the modernists stressed reason in interpreting religion but did not make it the only guide, since the tradition is faith-based.

dominated-front.rationale: Liberal Muslims embrace modernity and engagement with the West, while progressive anti-imperialist strands might support such a front.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: MPV commits to gender justice and women's full participation in public life.

ban-interest.rationale: Abduh and other modernists took a flexible view of interest, though the matter is contested.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth regardless of race and calls for dismantling structural racism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim held only by the socialist Shi'ite wing.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim incompatible with the equality and pluralism principles.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: MPV's equal worth principle rules out discouraging people from having children on grounds of heritable defect.

night-watchman-state.rationale: MPV's program of universal health care and public education requires more than a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth regardless of race and ethnicity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: MPV's Equality principle affirms the equal worth of all people, and Kurzman lists rights for women and non-Muslims as defining.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not directly addressed; post-colonial progressive Muslims may agree and others disagree.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Liberal Muslims cite 'no compulsion in religion' and MPV demands freedom of conscience in matters of faith.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not found in liberal Islamic sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Support for democracy is a defining liberal-Islamic position, and Abd al-Raziq argued caliphal rule had no divine basis.

population-transfer.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth regardless of creed and ethnicity and Kurzman stresses non-Muslim rights.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Compassion and cooperation, not competition and struggle, are named as the guiding principles.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: MPV condemns extremism but also defends free expression, so adherents are split on banning parties.

separated-powers.rationale: An-Na'im's constitutional-state model with human rights protections presupposes checks on power.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined vanguard cuts against the democratic and freedom-of-thought commitments.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: MPV embraces pluralism and diversity as positive values.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Substantive secular-state rights protections, as An-Na'im describes, apply even against majority will or state interest.

party-controls-media.rationale: MPV supports freedom of speech and nonviolent expression and dissent.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is incompatible with the constitutional democracy liberals support.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Neither the liberal Islamic thinkers nor MPV say anything about legislators' salaries, so adherents are indifferent.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kurzman defines liberal Islam by opposition to theocracy, and Soroush opposes rule by an official clerical ideology.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: MPV supports freedom of expression and opposes prosecuting people for ethical, law-abiding expression.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Liberal Islam depends on scholarly reinterpretation and does not hold this view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: MPV embraces pluralism and holds that one belief system is not the exclusive source of truth.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Abduh sought to reconcile Islam with modern science, and liberal Muslims generally accept evolution.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Freedom of conscience supports exemptions but equal law cuts against them.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: MPV values critical thinking and free expression, which supports non-conformity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Only the progressive anti-imperialist and socialist strands speak to it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberal Islam prizes freedom of thought and democracy and does not trade them for growth.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Abduh sought to end the ulama's monopoly on interpretation and Soroush wants clerical reform, implying civil authority over clergy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Abd al-Raziq argued that the Prophet held only spiritual leadership and that no scriptural basis exists for a sacral system of rule.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Constitutional democracy and rights protections, including against the state, are central to liberal Islam, and Abd al-Raziq rejected caliphs' violent, unaccountable rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a leader as the nation's embodiment is contrary to the democratic, anti-sacral commitments that define the tradition.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not found in the liberal strand.

land-redistribution.rationale: Only the socialist Shi'ite strand speaks to it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Liberal Muslims argue against any penalty for apostasy citing 'no compulsion in religion', and MPV condemns persecuting thinkers as apostates.

women-must-cover.rationale: Many progressives reject mandatory hijab and MPV asserts women's agency over their bodies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Abduh viewed ummah unity as moral, and nothing supports ethno-linguistic union.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist claim not held by liberal Muslims, who give ideas and ijtihad a central role.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: An-Na'im defines the secular state as one that protects rights even when they conflict with majority will.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: MPV rejects violence at every level, and liberal Islam relies on democratic reform.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: MPV's equal-worth principle opposes inherited privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Liberal and progressive Muslim thinkers are anti-colonial and affirm equal worth, which rejects tutelage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: MPV opposes structural racism but there is no documented stance on admissions preferences.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism can avoid collapse is a Marxist debate that liberal Islamic thinkers do not engage with.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim addressed only by the socialist strand.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: MPV's equality principle opposes discrimination by sex, race, creed or sexual orientation.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: An-Na'im's constitutional state protects human rights even against majority will.

elective-rulers.rationale: Support for democracy is a defining liberal-Islamic position, and Abd al-Raziq rejected any religious basis for hereditary or imposed caliphal rule.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: MPV stresses social engagement and justice.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Progressive anti-imperialist strand might agree but liberal modernists would not.

native-born-offices.rationale: MPV's equality principle includes nationality and rejects such discrimination.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal worth and equal political rights for all citizens tell against ancestry-based leadership.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Liberal Muslims oppose both totalitarian systems, but equating fascism and communism is a historical judgement the sources do not make.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Kurzman presents liberal Islam as a case that democratic institutions do fit Muslim societies.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political guardian role for the army is incompatible with civilian democratic government.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Confucian idea of filling posts by examination is not a liberal Islamic theme, and adherents favour elected office in politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Liberal NGOs such as Sisters in Islam depend on open civil society, so restrictions are unwelcome.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: MPV's emphasis on women's self-determination in reproduction tells against pronatalism.

job-guarantee.rationale: The sources commit to ending poverty but do not endorse an employer-of-last-resort scheme or reject it.

non-intervention.rationale: Universal rights and anti-imperial caution pull in opposite directions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: MPV's equality and pluralism principles reject such claims.

religious-nation.rationale: MPV rejects defining belonging by religion and Kurzman stresses equal rights for non-Muslims.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberal Muslims reject communist authoritarianism, but a call to defeat communism is a Cold War stance outside the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Adherents are believing Muslims who read religion as a source of ethical guidance, as Abduh and Soroush did.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Whether capitalism has been historically progressive is a Marxist framing the liberal Islamic sources do not use.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: MPV links gender justice to economic opportunity but does not call for systemic transformation.

majority-settlement.rationale: Equal-worth and minority-rights commitments oppose engineered settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: An Islamist 'third way' idea, and liberal Muslims are not agreed on it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: MPV supports full LGBTQ equality and liberal Muslim groups campaign against such laws.

suppress-opposition.rationale: MPV supports nonviolent expression and dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: MPV supports free speech and condemns persecution of critical thinkers, and liberal Muslims reject penalties for apostasy.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Kurzman defines liberal Islam by opposition to theocracy and support for democracy, rejecting religious tests of rulers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: MPV's Equality principle lists race, sex, gender, sexual orientation and ability together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: MPV commits to equality regardless of gender identity.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist idea addressed only by the socialist strand.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Kurzman's whole account of liberal Islam is that Islam can and does accommodate democracy, rights and liberty.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Abd al-Raziq argued the caliphate had no divine basis and the Prophet's authority was spiritual only, so political authority is human.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: MPV supports women's agency and Muslim liberals oppose hijab bans.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: MPV opposes violence but does not call for abolishing armies.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Elected, accountable government and Abd al-Raziq's rejection of caliphal legitimacy tell against hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Islamic banking is a concern of Islamists and liberals are split.

property-franchise.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth and political participation for all.

domination-women-nature.rationale: MPV supports both gender justice and environmental justice but does not link them.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Marxist critique of formal press freedom is not shared by the liberal strand, which values free speech as stated, but is also not rejected.

racial-franchise.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth regardless of race or ethnicity and full political participation.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: MPV supports interfaith marriage and liberal Muslims argue against restrictions, though traditional views remain strong in the milieu.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: MPV's equality and pluralism principles reject targeting a religious minority.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Liberal Islam's methodological core is ijtihad, reinterpreting Qur'an and law for modern conditions, as Abduh and Abu Zayd argued.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: MPV supports full LGBTQ equality and inclusion.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: MPV's freedom of conscience principle and the believers' own faith oppose state promotion of atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Liberal Muslims want a constitutional state with law enforcement and rights protections.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: MPV supports universal state provision such as health care and public education.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Amina Wadud, featured in Kurzman's anthology, argued for women's religious leadership and Unity Mosque is gender-equal.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: MPV's gender justice commitment and Abduh's opposition to polygamy point toward equal authority in marriage.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements contradict the commitments to free thought and democracy.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-imperial Muslims lean yes but modernist liberals are divided.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: MPV rejects violence but defensive force is accepted in Islamic ethics.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Liberal Islam emphasizes change and reinterpretation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: MPV supports gender-identity inclusion but liberal Islam takes no position on the social construction of biological sex.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring martyrs is part of Islamic tradition but MPV rejects glorifying violence.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: MPV warns against mixing religion and politics.

god-not-male.rationale: Progressive Muslim feminist theologians such as Wadud argue for gender-neutral language about God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: MPV calls for readings that reflect fairness and promote women's full participation.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: MPV's equality principle opposes giving the majority group economic control.

person-over-state.rationale: An-Na'im's rights-protecting secular state places the person's rights above state interest.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Liberal Muslims are religious, and Abduh and Soroush defend religion's role in human life, but politics serving spiritual ends conflicts with their secular tendency.

racial-group-interests.rationale: MPV affirms equal worth and rejects racial divisions.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: MPV rejects violence at the national level.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Abduh viewed ummah unity as moral, and liberals favour civic over ethnolinguistic nationhood.

free-public-college.rationale: MPV supports public education and economic opportunity.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: MPV supports women's participation but not gender essentialism.

arms-reduction.rationale: MPV rejects violence at the national level.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Liberal Islam works through constitutional democracy rather than the destruction of the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The sources set no economic blueprint, but they also do not endorse free experimentation between communities, so adherents are split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: MPV holds that one's belief system is not the exclusive source of truth.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: MPV commits to equal economic opportunity and women's agency, and liberal writers cited by Kurzman press for women's rights.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: An-Na'im argues that multiple interpretations undermine any single state-enforced shari'a, and Soroush rejects any official interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Liberal Muslims value democracy for rights and not only elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: MPV supports women's agency over sexuality, though broader liberal opinion is mixed.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: MPV supports free speech and dissent.

women-suffrage.rationale: MPV states support for women's full participation in political life, and Kurzman lists women's rights as defining.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Liberal Muslims hold that patriarchal readings, not Islam itself, oppress women, and offer egalitarian readings.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Abu Zayd treated the Qur'an as a historically situated text and MPV calls for critical engagement with scripture, rejecting literalism.

national-church-status.rationale: MPV's separation principle and equal treatment of beliefs oppose a privileged religious body.

simple-living.rationale: Islamic ethics values moderation, but the sources do not call for self-sufficient simple living as a political goal.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: A spiritual bond between a nation and its homeland is a nationalist theme absent from liberal Islamic thought.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Rights protections and the rule of law in An-Na'im's constitutional state forbid killings without trial.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Only socialist Shi'ite thinkers address common ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: MPV stresses bodily autonomy and individual self-determination.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Democratic party politics and civil society are central; bypassing them for a leader is rejected.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: MPV's separation principle and Kurzman's definition oppose religiously organized politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Modernists pursued modernity with Islamic roots, but liberal Muslims rarely call for a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: MPV's women's self-determination principle supports women initiating divorce.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: MPV rejects violence at every level, but a call for working people to seek their own government's defeat is a Leninist doctrine not found in liberal Islam.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Economics are unsettled in Islamic liberalism, ranging from social-democratic to market-friendly, so adherents are split.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The strand stresses equality and rights but does not address this empirical question about racial disadvantage.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Islamic liberals hold that religious or political authority must be democratic and rights-protecting, which conflicts with one-party rule.

missingStatements.text: The state should not enforce religious law on its citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: An-Na'im argues enforcement of shari'a by the state negates its religious character, and MPV holds secular government achieves freedom from compulsion in faith.

missingStatements.text: No caliph or religious office is required to govern a Muslim society.
missingStatements.rationale: Abd al-Raziq argued the caliphate was not an obligatory institution and Islam is mainly a faith, not a blueprint for government.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Islamic political thought; clerical-rule and laws-from-scripture already place the ideology.

missingStatements.text: Muslims should be free to leave Islam or change religion without penalty.
missingStatements.rationale: Liberal Muslims cite 'no compulsion in religion' against penalties for apostasy and MPV condemns persecuting critical thinkers as apostates.

notes: Contested: LGBTQ inclusion, abortion and premarital sex are affirmed by activist groups such as MPV but split the wider liberal mainstream. Economic questions are largely unaddressed; the Shi'ite socialist wing (Shariati, Taleghani) would answer them differently. No primary text was readable in full, so MPV's principles serve as the program source and thinkers' views come from reference and scholarly summaries.
